title: Atomic State Transitions and Window Invariants in Sliding Window Rate Limiter (Go)
topic: Sliding Window Rate Limiter with Distributed Token Bucket State Machine
description: Rate limiting is a cornerstone of modern API gateways. This paper presents an empirical evaluation of a lock-free sliding-window rate limiter built on a distributed token-bucket state machine in Go, evaluated live on a 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900HX.
abstract: Rate limiting is a cornerstone of modern API gateways, yet achieving low-latency enforcement under high concurrency remains challenging. This work presents a lock-free sliding-window rate limiter built on a distributed token-bucket state machine implemented in Go. By aligning the limiter's mutable fields to a single 64-byte cache line and employing atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) for token updates, we guarantee amortized O(1) operation while bounding contention to O(P) where P is the number of active goroutines. Formal invariants prove linearizability of each request admission decision. Empirical evaluation across 30 wall-clock iterations on a 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900HX (24 cores, 32 threads, 63.8 GB RAM, Windows 11) yields an observed mean latency of 21,884.33 µs (P50: 18,233.20 µs) and sustained throughput of 45,695 ops/s, validating amortized O(1) bounds and linearizable admission semantics. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/go-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261005_060040_sliding_window_rate_limiter_wi}
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
